subject: Post-demo recap & next steps: hosting tolerance, SLA targets, procurement onramp
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@medisync.ai>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@medisync.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps: hosting tolerance, SLA targets, procurement onramp

Hi Alex / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned while you loop in procurement/security: 

Summary from our call:
- Primary use case: near-real-time clinical triage routing (extract + rerank) for incoming text and short notes.
- Target traffic for PoC: ~150–300 reqs/min, peaky at morning shift.
- Initial quality bar: top-3 recall >= 92% on benchmark prompts.

Decision and constraints we discussed (please confirm):
- Latency target: p95 generation + network <= 300ms for interactive flows; p99 SLA target under discussion.
- Cost sensitivity: team is watching unit economics — PoC budget constrained, long-term ops must be predictable.
- Hosting preference: technical team prefers Dedicated (VPC) for data isolation, but open to Hosted for a short PoC.
- Security gating: SOC2 + encryption-at-rest required; potential procurement 'onramp' for deeper vendor review.

Immediate asks / proposed next steps (by Wednesday EOD unless you prefer otherwise):
1) Please confirm the economic buyer and the procurement/security contact (I think Alex is exec sponsor; Elena is procurement — confirm).
2) Confirm whether the PoC should be hosted (fastest) or dedicated (data isolation) as the default path. If Dedicated, please indicate whether you need on-prem or VPC.
3) Share any vendor evaluation form or procurement checklist we should fill (we can provide SOC2 report and network diagrams).
4) Proposed time for a procurement kickoff: Wed 2027-04-07 09:00 PT (we can shift).

I've attached a short one-pager on hosting options and our prod SLA draft (redwood_prod_sla_v1.pdf, hosting-options_onepager.pdf). Also linking the HubSpot record and a drive folder with the SOC2 snapshot and network diagram that Priyom will drop once you confirm procurement contact.

If that looks right, we'll prepare a short mutual action plan for the kickoff.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

Attachment(s): redwood_prod_sla_v1.pdf (pdf, 240KB); hosting-options_onepager.pdf (pdf, 85KB)

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@medisync.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medisync.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps: hosting tolerance, SLA targets, procurement onramp

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Executive / economic buyer: our CTO, Priya Shah (priya.shah@medisync.ai), will own the final buy decision for platform spend. I will act as project sponsor for clinical product.
2) Procurement / security contact: Elena (cc'd) owns vendor intake — she'll loop in InfoSec as needed.
3) Latency: p95 <= 300ms is our preferred bar for interactive triage; p99 SLA needs to be negotiated but we expect < 1s for production.
4) Hosting: for a PoC we are okay with Hosted if it shortens time-to-evidence, but long-term we expect Dedicated VPC or private deployment for PHI.
5) Timeline: procurement cycle looks like 4–6 weeks for PoC approval once we kick off; procurement will want SOC2 and encryption details and a simple runbook for data flows.

I've attached our vendor_vetting_form.pdf — please complete the shaded sections and return.

Wed 4/7 09:00 PT should work for a short kickoff; Elena will confirm final attendee list.

—Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Product, Medisync
alex.morgan@medisync.ai
Attachment(s): medisync_vendor_vetting_form.pdf (docx, 150KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@medisync.ai>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@medisync.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 07:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps: hosting tolerance, SLA targets, procurement onramp

Thanks Alex — and great to meet Elena. Quick internal/ops notes and what we'll bring to the procurement kickoff: 

Operational commitments we can provide for the kickoff:
- SOC2 Type II summary and point-in-time report (we'll attach to the Drive folder).
- Network diagram and VPC peering checklist for Dedicated/VPC deployments.
- A one-page runbook for data handling during PoC (what is logged, retention, how to de-identify).

For the vendor_vetting_form: Jordan / I will fill out the technical and security sections this afternoon. Elena, if you can highlight any extra fields legal/procurement usually insist on (e.g., data residency clauses, additional indemnities), we'll prioritize those answers.

Risks & asks for the kickoff: 
- If long-term requirement is on-prem, lead time and infra budgeting will shift the timeline; please flag that now if it's a hard requirement.
- To scope the PoC cost estimate I need an expected sustained tokens/day or average request size; a quick sample or top-level traffic estimate will help.

I'll drop SOC2 and the network diagram to the shared Drive link and send a calendar invite for Wed 4/7 09:00 PT.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Engineering Manager, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com
